failure_conditions: Use the explicit failed-attempt outcome and closing report in the current objective. An intention to withdraw, an unrelated side task or delegation alone does not satisfy it. An early departure leaves unplayed later objectives unfinished.
Resolve defeat, unconsciousness, death and recovery under the selected Ruleset and agreed boundaries; no scripted rescue cancels committed results.

gm_guidance.instructions:
Use this Plan as private preparation within Severed Lands. Ground play in the accepted party and starting facts. The named new people and incidents belong to this adventure; existing Setting facts and earned consequences remain authoritative. Give the player concrete information for a first decision, follow their chosen approach, and keep private answers concealed until discovered.

Make the named main problem and its leads accessible. Read the current act and all linked objective conditions before framing its main quest and reassess when a required result occurs. All listed conditions and the closing event are required; explicit alternatives satisfy only their own condition. Optional scenes can be deferred without adding gates. A completed side job does not replace the main story. Do not fabricate success or mark unplayed later acts complete after an early departure.
gm_guidance.player_freedom: Objectives express opportunities, not mandatory conduct. A refusal, changed allegiance or early discovery can change the route or end the job. Carry forward established consequences instead of restoring a preferred plot.
gm_guidance.preparation_detail: Read this preparation and its relevant Setting sources. Keep a concise record of named promises, discovered evidence, lost resources and NPC attitudes. The preparation contains the core answer and resolutions; incidental dialogue and connective description remain the GM’s work.
gm_guidance.railroading: Conclude after the bounded problem and immediate aftermath are resolved. Offer a short epilogue choice; begin a further adventure only if the player asks to continue.

facts.fact: A practice circle is marked beside Waystation’s yard. An audience has gathered for two voluntary exhibition bouts.
Organiser Fen Lark has training weapons and a healer on standby. No bout has begun and the player may ask to change or decline its terms.

advancement.allocation: The Player Character and Companions start and remain at level 2. Story success, defeat, combat and optional jobs never award advancement. Grant only the adventure's actually earned money, possessions and narrative rewards. Any lower-level encounter-variant notes are authoring guidance for a separately revised Plan, not permission to override this declaration in play.
advancement.timing: This edition stays at level 2 throughout its authored adventure and optional continuation. It awards no XP or level increases; changing that policy requires an explicitly revised Plan.

intended_player_experience: Two contrasting duels with agreed safety rules and no hidden lethal twist.

objectives.description: Complete or respectfully withdraw from the exhibition under agreed terms.
objectives.title: Two fair bouts

opening_direction: Start beside the marked exhibition circle as the organiser offers the player a place. Explain the victory and safety conditions before acceptance.
premise: A Lodge trainee owes the town an exhibition. Stand in for two friendly bouts and give the audience something worth remembering.

branches: Play to win through positioning and resource choices.
Ask for coaching, try a new approach and accept a sporting loss.
Renegotiate the second bout after a real injury or withdraw without a punitive ambush.
consequences: Dera remembers discipline or grace under defeat; Cal remembers showmanship or a clever move. These are social impressions, not forced allegiances.
Fen shares the fee and admits the injury publicly. A promised later lesson is an optional epilogue.
All linked objective conditions are required, including the named closing event. Carry optional promises forward; they neither replace nor extend this ending.
dynamic_encounter_guidance: Read the selected party before committing opposition. The written encounter is a suggested baseline, not automatic level scaling. Resolve checks, attacks, damage, resources and combat turns through the admitted D&D SRD Ruleset; narrate only committed results. Preserve negotiation, surrender, retreat and established positions.
planned_encounters: Bout one: Dera, baseline AC 13, HP 10, speed 30 ft, initiative +1, practice staff +3 to hit, 1d4+1 bludgeoning, one attack. First damaging hit ends the default bout before further exchanges; use standard committed attack results.

Bout two: Cal, baseline AC 12, HP 10, speed 30 ft, initiative +2, practice club +3 to hit, 1d4+1 bludgeoning, one attack. A legal shove uses the admitted Ruleset’s procedure. Neither opponent uses opportunity attacks after the referee has ended a bout. For experienced PCs, agree stronger opponents or handicaps openly before play; companions spectate or take their own separate voluntary match, not extra attacks in the duel.
situations: Character entry and scope. Recommended level 1–3; one player with zero to 2 optional companions. This is guidance, not an enforced level limit. The chosen character can accept the immediate invitation, negotiate terms or decline. Establish any needed local context openly without inventing prior player actions.

Fen Lark, trainee: promised an exhibition before discovering a wrist injury. They want the audience entertained, not fooled about who fights. They offer to share the 12 gp appearance fee regardless of the result.

First opponent Dera Flint: patient, courteous, testing distance and overextension. Second opponent Cal Moss: exuberant, quick to attempt a ring-out, watches the first bout to learn the player’s habits. Both stop on a clear yield.

Terms. Before combat, agree on first damaging hit, ring-out, or voluntary yield as the win condition; first hit is the default. Set a nonlethal presentation and use the engine’s actual hit-point and attack results. A healer being present is not authority to erase damage or restore spent resources. Allow real healing or rest through supported mechanics if needed between bouts, or end the exhibition early.

The circle. A twenty-foot chalk circle has level ground and no concealed hazards. Spectators remain outside a clear safety margin. A successful legal shove can win a ring-out bout when positioning supports it. Creative feints use supported checks or combat actions; applause does not grant an invented bonus.

Dera’s bout. She asks what the player hopes to learn and openly demonstrates her preferred guard. During the bout she holds distance and invites a risky approach. Afterward she offers one concrete observation based on what actually happened. If the player wins by an unexpected legal tactic, she praises that tactic rather than calling it cheating.

Cal’s bout. Cal copies or counters the tactic he saw, with no secret stat increase. He may announce a bold approach to encourage the crowd. If the player is hurt or tired, Cal offers first-touch terms or postponement. Fen resolves the fee after both bouts or an agreed cancellation; the event can end happily with losses on the scorecard.

unsupported_mechanics: The Plan does not implement new engine procedures. Its fictional deadlines, NPC attitudes, narrative projects and noncombat outcomes are GM adjudication; use existing Ruleset tools for encoded uncertainty and committed mechanical results.
Exhibition scoring and referee decisions are GM adjudication. Practice weapons still use declared attacks; do not promise damage immunity.
